id_scheme: SK-01..SK-44 are stable identifiers for the 44 roadmap skills, taken from the numbering both source sites already share. Project sprints are recorded separately and are not numbered as skills.

skills.name: Python Programming
skills.what_you_learn: variables, loops, functions, OOP, file I/O, modules, error handling, list comprehensions, virtual environments, package management with pip. The goal is to write clean, idiomatic Python that runs correctly and can be read by others.

intended_resources.title: Python Crash Course, 3rd Edition
intended_resources.rationale: The clearest beginner Python book in print. Covers all fundamentals through three complete projects (game, data viz, web app). Used in university intro CS courses worldwide. Don't substitute this.

intended_resources.title: CS50P — Introduction to Programming with Python
intended_resources.rationale: Best free Python course that exists. Problem sets are genuinely hard, feedback is immediate. The pacing and rigor are university-grade. Available entirely free on cs50.harvard.edu.

intended_resources.title: 100 Days of Code: The Complete Python Pro Bootcamp
intended_resources.rationale: Best paid Python course for project-based learners. 100 projects, builds habit through daily practice. Angela Yu's teaching style is exceptionally clear. ~$15–20 on Udemy sale.

study_plan.detail: Variables, types, operators, input/output, f-strings. Install Python, VSCode, venv.
if/elif/else, for loops, while loops, break/continue. Build 5 small programs.
def, args, kwargs, return, default params, scope, recursion basics, lambda.
Lists, tuples, dicts, sets — methods, comprehensions, slicing, nested structures.
Classes, __init__, attributes, methods, self. Build a Bank Account class.
Inheritance, polymorphism, dunder methods, properties, class vs instance attrs.
import, pip, venv, requirements.txt, __init__.py, building a package.
open(), read/write, with statement, try/except/finally, custom exceptions.
Generators, iterators, decorators, context managers, *args/**kwargs advanced.
Arrays, vectorized ops (NumPy). Series, DataFrame, read_csv, basic manipulation (pandas).
Build: CLI inventory manager with CSV persistence, OOP design, full error handling.
pytest basics, assertions, fixtures. Write tests for your inventory manager project.
Review all concepts. Refactor project. Solve 10 HackerRank Python challenges.

skills.name: SQL
skills.what_you_learn: SELECT, filtering, JOINs (inner/left/right/full), GROUP BY, aggregations, subqueries, CTEs (WITH clauses), window functions (ROW_NUMBER, LAG, LEAD, RANK), query optimization basics, indexes, and EXPLAIN plans.

intended_resources.title: Practical SQL, 2nd Edition
intended_resources.rationale: Uses real datasets (US census, crime data) to teach SQL through actual analysis. Covers PostgreSQL deeply including geospatial, full-text search, and performance tuning. The most practical SQL book in print.

intended_resources.title: SQLZoo + Mode SQL Tutorial
intended_resources.rationale: SQLZoo is the best interactive SQL practice environment for beginners. Mode's tutorial (mode.com/sql-tutorial) covers intermediate and advanced topics including window functions. Use both together.

intended_resources.title: SQL Fundamentals Track
intended_resources.rationale: Covers beginner through advanced SQL including window functions, query optimization, and database design. DataCamp's in-browser SQL editor means zero setup friction. Best for structured, guided SQL learning.

study_plan.detail: SELECT, FROM, WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT. Install PostgreSQL + pgAdmin. Load sample DB.
COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, GROUP BY, HAVING. Solve 20 SQLZoo exercises.
INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL OUTER, CROSS, SELF JOINs. Design a 3-table schema.
Correlated subqueries, EXISTS, IN, NOT IN, WITH (CTEs), recursive CTEs.
ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK, LAG, LEAD, PARTITION BY, running totals.
B-tree indexes, composite indexes, EXPLAIN ANALYZE, query planning basics.
Normalization (1NF–3NF), primary/foreign keys, constraints, transactions (ACID).
Views, materialized views, stored procedures, triggers, JSON in PostgreSQL.
psycopg2, SQLAlchemy ORM basics. Query a DB from Python. pandas read_sql().
Build: analytics report from a real Kaggle dataset. 20 complex queries. LeetCode SQL top-50.

skills.name: Linear Algebra
skills.what_you_learn: vectors and vector spaces, matrix operations (add, multiply, transpose), linear transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, matrix decomposition (SVD, PCA), dot products, norms, and how these operations map to neural network computations.

intended_resources.title: Mathematics for Machine Learning
intended_resources.rationale: The only math book that connects linear algebra directly to ML algorithms. Chapters 2–4 cover everything needed. Free legally at mml-book.github.io. Used at Imperial College London and Cambridge.

intended_resources.title: Essence of Linear Algebra
intended_resources.rationale: The best visual intuition for linear algebra ever made. 15 videos (~3hrs total). Every abstract concept is animated geometrically. Watch before reading the MML book — it makes the abstractions click immediately.

intended_resources.title: Mathematics for Machine Learning: Linear Algebra
intended_resources.rationale: Taught by David Dye of Imperial College. Builds directly toward ML applications. Includes programming assignments in Python/NumPy. Best structured paid course connecting math to ML code.

study_plan.detail: Vector spaces, operations, dot product, norms. 3B1B videos Ch.1–3. NumPy implementation.
Matrix addition, multiplication, transpose. 3B1B Ch.4–5. Implement matrix multiply from scratch.
Geometric meaning of matrices, basis change, determinants. 3B1B Ch.6–7.
Solving Ax=b, Gaussian elimination, inverse matrices, rank, null space. MML Book Ch.2.
Eigendecomposition, characteristic polynomial, diagonalization. 3B1B Ch.14.
Singular Value Decomposition, PCA for dimensionality reduction. Implement PCA in NumPy.
How linear algebra maps to neural nets, word embeddings, attention. Consolidation + review.

skills.name: Probability & Statistics
skills.what_you_learn: probability rules, conditional probability, Bayes' theorem, common distributions (Normal, Binomial, Poisson), expectation and variance, hypothesis testing, p-values, confidence intervals, maximum likelihood estimation, and statistical intuition for ML models.

intended_resources.title: Naked Statistics: Stripping the Dread from the Data
intended_resources.rationale: Builds genuine statistical intuition without calculus. After Naked Statistics, pair with StatQuest's videos for the ML-specific depth. This book removes the fear of statistics before you need to formalize it.

intended_resources.title: StatQuest with Josh Starmer
intended_resources.rationale: The single best free resource for statistics and ML concepts. Every video explains one concept from first principles with custom visuals. Covers Bayes, distributions, hypothesis testing, and all ML-relevant stats. Hundreds of free videos.

intended_resources.title: Statistics with Python Specialization
intended_resources.rationale: 3-course specialization covering understanding, visualizing, and inferential statistics — all implemented in Python. Bridges statistical theory to Python code in a way most courses skip. Strong capstone project.

study_plan.detail: Sample spaces, events, addition rule, multiplication rule, independence. StatQuest: Probability videos.
Conditional probability, Bayes theorem, prior/posterior/likelihood, naive Bayes intuition.
Normal, Bernoulli, Binomial, Poisson, Exponential. Plot each with SciPy. Understand CLT.
Mean, median, mode, variance, std dev, skewness, kurtosis, quartiles, box plots.
t-tests, p-values, significance levels, Type I/II errors, confidence intervals. StatQuest series.
Maximum Likelihood Estimation, Maximum A Posteriori, how these underlie ML training.
Exploratory data analysis on a real dataset. Apply all stats concepts. StatQuest final review.

skills.name: Git & Version Control
skills.what_you_learn: init, add, commit, push/pull, branches, merge vs rebase, resolving conflicts, pull request workflow, cherry-pick, interactive rebase, stash, tags, GitHub/GitLab best practices, commit message conventions, and .gitignore strategies.

intended_resources.title: Pro Git, 2nd Edition
intended_resources.author_year: Scott Chacon & Ben Straub · Free at git-scm.com
intended_resources.rationale: The official, comprehensive Git reference. Written by GitHub co-founders. Covers everything from basics to Git internals. Completely free online at git-scm.com/book. Chapter 2 alone is worth more than most Git courses.

intended_resources.title: Learn Git Branching (Interactive)
intended_resources.rationale: Best interactive Git visualizer in existence. Every branch, merge, and rebase is animated in real-time. Builds muscle memory for complex workflows. Free. No install. 30 levels of increasing complexity.

intended_resources.title: Git & GitHub — The Complete Git Guide
intended_resources.rationale: Covers Git from zero to advanced workflows including rebase strategies, team workflows, GitHub Actions integration, and real project scenarios. Schwarzmüller's explanations are exceptionally structured. Best for learning team Git workflows.

study_plan.detail: init, add, commit, log, diff, stash, .gitignore. Learn Git Branching (all basic levels).
Branch, merge, rebase, cherry-pick, conflict resolution. Finish Learn Git Branching advanced levels.
Fork, PR, code review, GitHub flow, semantic commits, tagging releases. Push all prior projects.

skills.name: Linux / Command Line
skills.what_you_learn: filesystem navigation, file manipulation (cp/mv/rm/chmod), pipes and redirection, grep/awk/sed, environment variables, bash scripting (conditionals, loops, functions), process management (ps/kill/top), SSH, cron jobs, and package management (apt/brew).

intended_resources.title: The Linux Command Line, 2nd Edition
intended_resources.rationale: The most complete introduction to the Linux CLI. Covers shells, scripting, package management, and system administration. Completely free online at linuxcommand.org. Used as the standard reference in Linux sysadmin courses.

intended_resources.title: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education
intended_resources.rationale: The most practical CS skills course that universities don't teach. Covers shell, Vim, Git, tmux, SSH, and debugging tools in 12 focused lectures. All free. Every professional engineer eventually finds this and wishes they had it earlier.

intended_resources.title: Linux Command Line Bootcamp: Beginner to Power User
intended_resources.rationale: Colt Steele's teaching clarity is exceptional. Covers all practical Linux skills with real-world exercises and a built-in terminal emulator. Best for learners who want structured progression with video explanation.

study_plan.detail: pwd, ls, cd, mkdir, rm, cp, mv, find, chmod, chown. MIT Missing Semester Lectures 1–2.
pipe |, redirect >, grep, awk, sed, sort, uniq, wc, cut, xargs. Process 3 real CSV files.
Variables, loops, conditions, functions in bash. Write 5 automation scripts. cron jobs.
SSH keygen, remote login, tmux, ps, kill, top, htop, env vars, systemd basics.

skills.name: Data Structures
skills.what_you_learn: arrays, dynamic arrays, linked lists (single/double), stacks, queues, hash maps, sets, trees (binary, BST, AVL), heaps (min/max), graphs (adjacency list/matrix), tries, and when to use each. Implement from scratch in Python before using built-ins.

intended_resources.title: Introduction to Algorithms (CLRS), 4th Edition
intended_resources.rationale: The canonical algorithms textbook. Used at MIT, Stanford, CMU. Chapters 10–14 cover all fundamental data structures with full proofs. Don't read cover-to-cover — use it as a reference and study specific chapters.

intended_resources.title: NeetCode Data Structures & Algorithms for Beginners
intended_resources.rationale: Best free visual DSA course for interview preparation. Each video covers one structure with code implementation and complexity analysis. Pairs perfectly with LeetCode. NeetCode's animations make abstract structures concrete instantly.

intended_resources.title: Python Data Structures & Algorithms + LEETCODE Exercises
intended_resources.rationale: The most complete paid DSA course using Python. Every data structure is implemented from scratch with full explanation. Includes 100+ LeetCode problems mapped to each structure. Best for building a complete, tested implementation library.

study_plan.detail: Dynamic arrays, amortized cost, string immutability. Implement ArrayList in Python. 5 LeetCode Easy.
Singly + doubly linked lists from scratch. Insertion, deletion, reversal. 5 LeetCode problems.
Stack (LIFO), Queue (FIFO), Deque, implement with linked list and array. 5 LeetCode problems.
Hash functions, collision handling (chaining/open addressing), implement HashMap. 5 LeetCode.
Binary trees, BST insert/delete/search, in/pre/post-order traversal. 5 LeetCode tree problems.
AVL trees concept, Red-Black trees concept, Min/Max Heap, heap operations, heapq. 5 LeetCode.
Adjacency list/matrix, directed/undirected, weighted graphs. Implement graph class. 5 LeetCode.
Trie implementation, insert/search/startsWith. Use cases (autocomplete). 3 LeetCode Trie problems.
When to use which structure. Time/space complexity table. Solve 10 mixed LeetCode Easy.
2 timed problems (45 min each). Practice explaining your approach out loud.

skills.name: Algorithms & Big-O
skills.what_you_learn: time and space complexity analysis, O(1)/O(log n)/O(n)/O(n log n)/O(n²) intuition, sorting algorithms (merge, quick, heap), searching (binary search, BFS, DFS), dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, backtracking, and two-pointer / sliding window patterns.

intended_resources.title: Grokking Algorithms, 2nd Edition
intended_resources.rationale: The most approachable algorithms book ever written. Every algorithm is illustrated with hand-drawn visuals. Covers Big-O, recursion, dynamic programming, and graphs. Read this before CLRS — it builds the right mental models first.

intended_resources.title: 6.006 — Introduction to Algorithms
intended_resources.rationale: Free MIT algorithm lectures. Full lecture videos, problem sets, and exams. The most rigorous free algorithms course available. Taught by Erik Demaine (MIT). Covers sorting, hashing, dynamic programming, and graph algorithms with proofs.

intended_resources.title: AlgoExpert — Algorithms & Coding Interview Prep
intended_resources.rationale: 160+ curated algorithm problems with video explanations (not just solutions). Every problem comes with a walkthrough of the thought process. Best for systematically preparing for technical interviews while learning algorithms simultaneously.

study_plan.detail: Time/space complexity, O(1)/O(log n)/O(n)/O(n log n)/O(n²). Analyze 20 code snippets.
Bubble, Selection, Insertion, Merge Sort, Quick Sort. Implement all 5 in Python. Compare.
Iterative + recursive binary search, search on answer concept. 8 LeetCode binary search problems.
BFS (queue-based), DFS (stack/recursive), level-order traversal. 8 LeetCode graph problems.
Two-pointer technique, fixed/variable sliding window. 8 LeetCode Medium problems using patterns.
Greedy choice property, interval scheduling, activity selection. 6 LeetCode Greedy.
Recursion trees, memoization intro, backtracking template. N-Queens, permutations, subsets.
Memoization vs tabulation, 1D DP problems: Fibonacci, climbing stairs, coin change.
2D DP: longest common subsequence, edit distance, knapsack. Recognize DP patterns.
Dijkstra's (shortest path), Bellman-Ford, Topological sort, Union-Find (DSU). 6 LeetCode.
Categorize 50 LeetCode problems by pattern. Build a personal cheat sheet.
3 timed LeetCode Medium problems. Record yourself explaining. Simulate FAANG conditions.

skills.name: Design Patterns & SOLID
skills.what_you_learn: SOLID principles (Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion), GoF patterns (Factory, Strategy, Observer, Decorator, Singleton, Command, Adapter, Facade), and when to apply or intentionally avoid each.

intended_resources.title: Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship
intended_resources.rationale: Sets the professional standard for code quality and SOLID principles. The SOLID chapter alone transforms how you write code. Read once, re-read every 2 years. Every senior engineer at FAANG references this implicitly in code reviews.

intended_resources.title: ArjanCodes — Design Patterns in Python
intended_resources.rationale: Best free Python-specific design patterns resource. Arjan implements every GoF pattern and SOLID principle in real Python projects, showing both the before and after refactor. Shows patterns in the context of realistic code, not toy examples.

intended_resources.title: Design Patterns in Python
intended_resources.rationale: All 23 GoF patterns implemented in Python with real-world use cases. Nesteruk provides clear rationale for when to use each pattern and the anti-patterns to avoid. Most complete paid design patterns course for Python developers.

study_plan.detail: SRP, OCP, LSP, ISP, DIP — one principle per 1.5 hrs with before/after code examples.
Factory Method, Abstract Factory, Builder, Singleton, Prototype. Implement each in Python.
Adapter, Facade, Decorator, Composite, Bridge, Proxy, Flyweight. Real-world examples.
Observer, Strategy, Command, Iterator, State, Template Method, Chain of Responsibility.
Take 3 "bad code" examples, identify smells, apply patterns to fix. ArjanCodes exercises.
Build a plugin system using Strategy + Factory + Observer patterns combined.

skills.name: Web Frameworks (FastAPI / Django)
skills.what_you_learn: RESTful API design, routing, request/response lifecycle, middleware, dependency injection (FastAPI), ORM and database migrations, authentication/sessions, background tasks, OpenAPI/Swagger auto-docs, and deploying Python web apps to production.

intended_resources.title: FastAPI: Modern Python Web Development
intended_resources.rationale: FastAPI is the current industry standard for Python APIs (used at Uber, Netflix, Microsoft). This book covers async APIs, database integration, authentication, testing, and deployment end-to-end. FastAPI is the right default in 2024 — learn it over Django for new API projects.

intended_resources.title: FastAPI Official Tutorial & Documentation
intended_resources.rationale: The FastAPI docs are so well-written they function as a course. Tiangolo (creator) wrote them to be tutorial-quality. The tutorial section alone covers 80% of what you need. Frequently cited as the best framework documentation in Python.

intended_resources.title: FastAPI — The Complete Course 2024 (Beginner + Advanced)
intended_resources.rationale: Full coverage from routing through JWT auth, PostgreSQL integration, Docker deployment, and testing. Builds a complete production-ready application. Best structured video course for FastAPI in a real production context.

study_plan.detail: Routes, path/query params, request bodies (Pydantic models), response models, status codes.
SQLAlchemy + FastAPI, async sessions, CRUD operations, migration with Alembic.
JWT tokens, OAuth2 password flow, password hashing (bcrypt), protected endpoints.
CORS, custom middleware, background tasks, WebSockets intro, lifespan events.
TestClient, pytest for FastAPI, mocking DB, test fixtures, 100% coverage on a small API.
Full CRUD API: users, items, auth, DB, tests. Like a mini e-commerce backend.
Dockerize the API. Deploy to Railway/Fly.io/Render. Add health check endpoint.
Dependency injection, custom exception handlers, OpenAPI docs, versioning. Review.

skills.name: Testing & TDD
skills.what_you_learn: unit vs integration vs end-to-end tests, pytest fixtures, parametrize, mocking with unittest.mock, test coverage, property-based testing with Hypothesis, TDD red-green-refactor cycle, testing FastAPI/Django endpoints, and writing tests that don't break with every refactor.

intended_resources.title: Python Testing with pytest, 2nd Edition
intended_resources.rationale: The most complete pytest reference available. Covers fixtures, plugins, parametrization, mocking, and integration testing. Brian Okken created the Python Test Podcast. After this book, pytest has no surprises for you.

intended_resources.title: Unit Testing and TDD in Python — ArjanCodes
intended_resources.rationale: Best free TDD tutorial for Python engineers. Arjan shows the full TDD cycle on real Python projects, demonstrates common pitfalls, and explains what makes a good test vs a brittle one. Several videos covering different testing patterns.

intended_resources.title: Test-Driven Development with FastAPI and Docker
intended_resources.rationale: Builds a complete FastAPI application using strict TDD from the first line of code. Covers pytest, mocking, test containerization, and CI integration. Best paid resource for TDD in a production Python context. ~$40 one-time.

study_plan.detail: Fixtures, parametrize, markers, conftest.py, temp files, capsys. 20 testing exercises.
unittest.mock, MagicMock, patch decorators, mocking HTTP calls, mocking DB.
Full TDD cycle on a new feature. Write failing test first, implement, refactor. 3 complete cycles.
Testing database interactions, API integration tests with real DB, test containers.
pytest-cov for coverage, add tests to GitHub Actions CI pipeline. Aim 90%+ coverage.

skills.name: Docker & Kubernetes
skills.what_you_learn: Dockerfile authoring, image layers, docker-compose for multi-service apps, container networking, volumes, environment management, Kubernetes pods/deployments/services, ConfigMaps/Secrets, ingress controllers, resource limits, and basic cluster operations with kubectl.

intended_resources.title: Docker Deep Dive
intended_resources.rationale: The most concise, complete Docker book available. Poulton also wrote "The Kubernetes Book" — buy both. Clear explanations of images, containers, networking, and compose. Readable in a weekend, comprehensive enough to last years.

intended_resources.title: Docker Training Course for the Absolute Beginner
intended_resources.rationale: KodeKloud's free Docker course includes interactive labs in a real browser-based environment — no local Docker install needed. Best for hands-on learning without setup friction. Mumshad is known for the CKA Kubernetes certification course.

intended_resources.title: Docker & Kubernetes: The Practical Guide (2024)
intended_resources.rationale: Covers Docker and Kubernetes together in one course — the only pair that makes sense since Kubernetes orchestrates Docker containers. Builds a complete multi-service application. Most comprehensive paid course combining both tools with practical projects.

study_plan.detail: Images, containers, Dockerfile, layers, CMD vs ENTRYPOINT. Containerize your FastAPI app.
Multi-service apps: API + DB + Redis. Networking, volumes, env files, health checks.
Multi-stage builds, image optimization, push to Docker Hub / GitHub Container Registry.
Pods, ReplicaSets, Deployments, Services (ClusterIP/NodePort/LoadBalancer). minikube setup.
ConfigMaps, Secrets, PersistentVolumes, StatefulSets. Deploy FastAPI + PostgreSQL on K8s.
Ingress controllers (NGINX), HPA (Horizontal Pod Autoscaler), resource limits, liveness probes.
Deploy complete app (API + DB + frontend) to K8s. Write YAML manifests from scratch.

skills.name: CI/CD Pipelines
skills.what_you_learn: GitHub Actions workflow YAML, triggers (push/PR/schedule), job dependencies, secrets management, build-test-deploy automation, Docker image build and push, environment-specific deployments, rollback strategies, and blue-green/canary deployment concepts.

intended_resources.title: Learning GitHub Actions
intended_resources.rationale: The most complete GitHub Actions reference. Covers workflows, runners, reusable actions, secrets, environments, and deployment automation. GitHub Actions is the dominant CI/CD tool for new projects. This book covers everything from basic pipelines to complex matrix builds.

intended_resources.title: GitHub Actions Official Documentation + TechWorld with Nana
intended_resources.rationale: GitHub's own docs are tutorial-quality. Pair with TechWorld with Nana's CI/CD YouTube series for visual walkthroughs. Nana covers GitHub Actions, Jenkins, and ArgoCD in the context of real DevOps workflows. Free and regularly updated.

intended_resources.title: GitHub Actions — The Complete Guide
intended_resources.rationale: Builds real CI/CD pipelines for Node, Python, and Docker projects. Covers caching, reusable workflows, matrix strategies, and deployment to cloud providers. Best structured video course for GitHub Actions in production contexts.

study_plan.detail: Workflow YAML, triggers, jobs, steps, runners. Build lint + test pipeline for your API project.
Matrix builds, caching (pip/npm), secrets management, environment-specific deployments.
Build Docker image in CI, push to registry, deploy to staging on PR merge.
Full pipeline: lint → test → build → push → deploy → notify. Add to existing project.

skills.name: Security (OWASP / Auth)
skills.what_you_learn: OWASP Top 10 (injection, XSS, broken auth, IDOR, etc.), JWT structure and validation, OAuth 2.0 flows, API key management, password hashing (bcrypt/argon2), HTTPS/TLS basics, CORS, input validation/sanitization, and secure coding practices.

intended_resources.title: The Web Application Hacker's Handbook, 2nd Ed.
intended_resources.rationale: Understanding attacks is the prerequisite for defense. This book explains every web vulnerability from the attacker's perspective — teaching you exactly how SQL injection, XSS, and CSRF work so you can eliminate them. The most direct path to security thinking.

intended_resources.title: PortSwigger Web Security Academy
intended_resources.rationale: The best free web security training resource in existence. Built by the creators of Burp Suite. Covers every OWASP vulnerability with interactive labs where you actually exploit the vulnerability to understand how to prevent it. Completely free.

intended_resources.title: Web Security & Bug Bounty: Learn Penetration Testing
intended_resources.rationale: Practical offensive security course covering XSS, SQL injection, CSRF, file upload vulnerabilities, and authentication flaws — all in controlled lab environments. Best paid course for engineers who want to understand attacks before defending against them.

study_plan.detail: SQL injection, XSS, CSRF, SSRF, broken auth. PortSwigger labs for each. Exploit then patch.
Session vs JWT vs OAuth2. bcrypt/argon2. Refresh tokens. Implement from scratch in FastAPI.
Rate limiting, API keys, CORS, HTTPS/TLS, input validation, parameterized queries.
OAuth2 flows (code, implicit, client credentials). Add "Login with Google" to FastAPI app.
Audit your existing projects for vulnerabilities. Run bandit (Python security linter). Fix all issues.

skills.name: Async Programming
skills.what_you_learn: Python asyncio, async/await syntax, event loops, coroutines vs threads vs processes, concurrent.futures, aiohttp for async HTTP, async database drivers, task groups, semaphores for concurrency limiting, and when to use async vs threading vs multiprocessing.

intended_resources.title: Using Asyncio in Python
intended_resources.rationale: The clearest explanation of Python's asyncio model. Hattingh removes the confusion around async/await, event loops, and coroutines. Short and focused — 150 pages that eliminate the fog around async Python better than any tutorial.

intended_resources.title: Asyncio in Python — mCoding YouTube Series
intended_resources.rationale: The most technically accurate free asyncio resource. James Murphy (PhD mathematician, senior engineer) explains Python's async model precisely, including the differences between coroutines, tasks, and futures. Zero hand-waving.

intended_resources.title: Concurrency & Multithreading in Python (threading, asyncio, multiprocessing)
intended_resources.rationale: Covers threading, multiprocessing, and asyncio together — which is essential because the choice between them determines performance. Best paid course for understanding Python concurrency as a whole system, not just asyncio in isolation.

study_plan.detail: Event loop, coroutines, tasks, futures. asyncio.run(), gather(), create_task(). mCoding videos.
aiohttp for async HTTP calls, asyncpg for async PostgreSQL. Build async data fetcher.
GIL limitations, threading for I/O-bound, multiprocessing for CPU-bound. concurrent.futures.
Celery + Redis for async task queues. Background jobs, retries, monitoring with Flower.
Fully async FastAPI with async DB, async external calls, WebSocket endpoint. Benchmark vs sync.

skills.name: System Design
skills.what_you_learn: load balancing (L4/L7), horizontal vs vertical scaling, caching strategies (CDN, Redis, write-through/around/back), database sharding, consistent hashing, CAP theorem, SQL vs NoSQL trade-offs, message queues, rate limiting, and designing real systems (URL shortener, YouTube, Twitter).

intended_resources.title: System Design Interview: An Insider's Guide (Vol 1 & 2)
intended_resources.rationale: The industry standard prep resource for system design interviews at FAANG. Vol 1 covers foundational patterns; Vol 2 covers advanced designs (Google Maps, Nearby Friends, distributed message queues). Buy both. Read before any senior SWE interview.

intended_resources.title: System Design Primer
intended_resources.rationale: 250k+ GitHub stars. The most comprehensive free system design resource. Covers every concept with diagrams, trade-off analysis, and links to source material. Used by engineers at every major company to prepare for system design rounds.

intended_resources.title: Grokking Modern System Design Interview
intended_resources.rationale: Interactive text-based course with diagrams for 20+ real system designs. Includes mock interview scenarios and structured frameworks for the interview itself. Best paid resource for building a systematic, repeatable approach to system design interviews.

study_plan.detail: Vertical vs horizontal scaling, load balancers (L4/L7), stateless services, CAP theorem.
Cache aside, write-through, write-back, CDN, Redis caching, cache invalidation strategies.
Read replicas, sharding, consistent hashing, connection pooling, SQL vs NoSQL decisions.
Full design session (1.5hr): requirements → API → DB → scale → deep dive. System Design Primer.
Photo storage, feed generation (push/pull model), notification system, CDN strategy.
WebSockets, message storage, presence service, group chats. Alex Xu Vol.1 Ch.12.
Video upload pipeline, transcoding, CDN, view counting at scale, recommendation hooks.
Token bucket, leaky bucket, sliding window algorithms. Distributed rate limiting with Redis.
When to split, service mesh, API gateway patterns, event-driven architecture, CQRS basics.
2 full 45-min design sessions with timer. Record and review. Write post-mortem.

skills.name: Apache Spark / PySpark
skills.what_you_learn: Spark architecture (driver/executors/DAG), RDDs vs DataFrames vs Datasets, transformations vs actions, lazy evaluation, PySpark DataFrame API, Spark SQL, partitioning strategies, shuffle optimization, reading/writing Parquet/Delta, and running Spark on YARN/Kubernetes.

intended_resources.title: Learning Spark: Lightning-Fast Data Analytics, 2nd Ed.
intended_resources.author_year: Damji, Wenig, Das & Lee · 2020 · Free PDF from Databricks
intended_resources.rationale: Written by Databricks engineers (who built Spark). Covers Spark 3.0, DataFrames, Spark SQL, structured streaming, and Delta Lake. Free PDF available from databricks.com/resources/ebook/learning-spark-lightning-fast-data-analytics. The definitive Spark reference.

intended_resources.title: Data Engineering Zoomcamp — Spark Module
intended_resources.rationale: Best free hands-on Spark course available. Part of the full Data Engineering Zoomcamp. Teaches PySpark through a real project pipeline. All materials, videos, and Jupyter notebooks are free on GitHub. Community Discord for Q&A.

intended_resources.title: Apache Spark 3 & Python 3 — Hands On with Big Data!
intended_resources.rationale: Frank Kane worked at Amazon building large-scale recommendation systems. This course covers Spark 3 from basics to MLlib and streaming. Best paid Spark course for engineers coming from a Python/data background. Practical focus throughout.

skills.name: Apache Kafka
skills.what_you_learn: Kafka architecture (brokers, topics, partitions, offsets), producer/consumer APIs, consumer groups, replication and fault tolerance, Kafka Connect for source/sink connectors, Kafka Streams for lightweight stream processing, schema registry with Avro, and deploying Kafka with Docker.

intended_resources.title: Kafka: The Definitive Guide, 2nd Edition
intended_resources.rationale: Written by Confluent engineers (who built commercial Kafka). Covers architecture, producers, consumers, streams, Connect, and operations. Free PDF available on Confluent's website. The authoritative reference for Kafka engineering.

intended_resources.title: Apache Kafka 101 — Confluent Developer Course
intended_resources.rationale: Official Kafka courses from the company that maintains it. "Apache Kafka 101" is the best starting point — covers all core concepts with short, focused video lessons and interactive exercises. Free. No registration required to access most content.

intended_resources.title: Apache Kafka Series — Learn Apache Kafka for Beginners v3
intended_resources.rationale: Maarek is a Confluent Kafka Certified Engineer and the most trusted Kafka instructor on Udemy. His entire Kafka series (Beginners → Streams → Connect → Schema Registry) is the de facto learning path. Best-in-class paid Kafka curriculum, start with Beginners v3.

skills.name: Data Warehouses (Snowflake / BigQuery / Redshift)
skills.what_you_learn: MPP (massively parallel processing) architecture, columnar storage, partitioning and clustering, query optimization for analytical workloads, virtual warehouses (Snowflake), materialized views, Time Travel, data sharing, cost optimization, and warehouse vs data lake trade-offs.

intended_resources.title: Snowflake: The Definitive Guide
intended_resources.rationale: Snowflake holds the largest market share in cloud data warehousing. Avila covers architecture, virtual warehouses, semi-structured data, performance tuning, and security. Snowflake proficiency is the most marketable DE skill in 2024 — this is the book to own it.

intended_resources.title: Snowflake University + Google BigQuery free tier
intended_resources.rationale: Snowflake University offers free certification prep courses. "Badge 1: Data Warehousing Workshop" covers all core concepts. Pair with Google's BigQuery sandbox (free tier, no credit card needed) for hands-on practice. Both are free with account creation.

intended_resources.title: Complete Snowflake Masterclass: Zero to Hero
intended_resources.rationale: Comprehensive Snowflake course covering architecture, SQL, performance optimization, dbt integration, and Snowpark (Python in Snowflake). Regularly updated for Snowflake's rapid feature releases. Best single paid resource for practical Snowflake engineering.

skills.name: ETL / ELT Pipelines
skills.what_you_learn: ETL vs ELT architectural differences, incremental vs full-load strategies, idempotency and exactly-once semantics, CDC (change data capture), Airbyte and Fivetran for ingestion, data lineage, backfilling strategies, error handling and dead-letter queues, and pipeline observability.

intended_resources.title: Fundamentals of Data Engineering
intended_resources.rationale: Chapters 8–9 cover the full data ingestion and transformation lifecycle in depth. This book defines the modern DE field. The pipeline design chapters are the best treatment of ETL/ELT patterns written for practitioners — not academics.

intended_resources.title: Data Engineering Zoomcamp — Full Pipeline Module
intended_resources.rationale: Best free end-to-end pipeline course. Builds a complete ETL pipeline from ingestion (Postgres → GCS/S3) through transformation (dbt) to serving (BigQuery). All code, videos, and homework on GitHub. Completely free.

intended_resources.title: The Complete Hands-On Introduction to Apache Airflow
intended_resources.rationale: Covers the full pipeline orchestration picture: Airflow DAGs, sensors, hooks, XCom, TaskFlow API, and best practices for production pipelines. Lamberti is the most respected Airflow instructor. Best paid course for building orchestrated ETL pipelines end-to-end.

skills.name: Apache Airflow
skills.what_you_learn: DAG structure (operators, tasks, dependencies), TaskFlow API, schedulers, sensors (FileSensor, HttpSensor), hooks (database connections), XCom for task communication, dynamic DAGs, testing DAGs with pytest, deploying on Docker/K8s, and Airflow 2.x best practices.

intended_resources.title: Data Pipelines with Apache Airflow
intended_resources.rationale: The only comprehensive Airflow book in print. Covers DAG design patterns, testing, scaling, and real production deployments. Includes chapters on Kubernetes executor and cloud deployment. The reference book for serious Airflow engineering.

intended_resources.title: Astronomer Academy — Airflow Fundamentals (Free)
intended_resources.rationale: Astronomer is the commercial company behind Apache Airflow. Their free courses and webinars are authoritative. The "Airflow Fundamentals" certification prep course is free and covers everything from DAG basics to production deployment patterns.

intended_resources.title: The Complete Hands-On Course to Master Apache Airflow
intended_resources.rationale: Marc Lamberti is the Airflow community's most recognized instructor. This course covers Airflow 2.x, TaskFlow API, custom operators, testing, and Kubernetes deployment. The de facto standard paid Airflow course — 50,000+ students.

skills.name: dbt (data build tool)
skills.what_you_learn: dbt project structure, models (SQL SELECT statements as tables/views), ref() and source() macros, materializations (table/view/incremental/ephemeral), tests (unique, not_null, accepted_values, relationships), documentation, Jinja templating, seeds, snapshots, and dbt Cloud vs dbt Core.

intended_resources.title: Analytics Engineering with SQL and dbt
intended_resources.rationale: The most complete dbt book. Covers the full analytics engineering workflow from raw data to final BI models using dbt. Includes real project walkthroughs with Snowflake and BigQuery. The best resource for learning dbt in a production analytics context.

intended_resources.title: dbt Fundamentals — Official dbt Course
intended_resources.rationale: Official free course by dbt Labs (who built dbt). Covers models, sources, tests, documentation, and deployment. Includes hands-on exercises in dbt Cloud. The "dbt Fundamentals" certification from this course is recognized in job postings. Completely free.

intended_resources.title: Complete dbt (Data Build Tool) Bootcamp: Zero to Hero
intended_resources.rationale: Builds a complete dbt project on Snowflake from scratch, covering advanced features like packages, hooks, macros, and CI/CD integration. Best paid course for engineers building production-grade dbt projects end-to-end.

skills.name: Dimensional Modeling (Kimball)
skills.what_you_learn: fact vs dimension tables, star schema vs snowflake schema, slowly changing dimensions (SCD Types 1/2/3), grain definition, degenerate dimensions, junk dimensions, date dimensions, bridge tables, factless fact tables, and the Kimball lifecycle methodology.

intended_resources.title: The Data Warehouse Toolkit, 3rd Edition
intended_resources.rationale: The Bible of dimensional modeling. 25 years old, still the definitive reference used by every data warehouse architect. Covers retail, procurement, HR, education, and healthcare schemas. Don't skim — every page is applicable to real projects.

intended_resources.title: Kahan Data Solutions — Dimensional Modeling Series
intended_resources.rationale: Best free visual introduction to dimensional modeling and data vault. Clear explanations of star schemas, SCD types, and real modeling decisions with diagrams. Pairs perfectly with the Kimball book by visualizing concepts that the book describes in text.

intended_resources.title: Data Warehouse — The Ultimate Guide
intended_resources.rationale: Covers dimensional modeling, data vault, and modern cloud warehouse implementation using Snowflake and dbt. Includes hands-on schema design exercises for multiple business domains. Best paid course connecting Kimball theory to modern cloud warehouse implementation.

skills.name: NoSQL Databases
skills.what_you_learn: document stores (MongoDB — CRUD, aggregation pipeline, indexing), wide-column stores (Cassandra — CQL, partition key design, replication), key-value stores (Redis — data types, TTL, pub/sub, caching patterns), and the CAP theorem trade-offs that determine which to use.

intended_resources.title: Seven Databases in Seven Weeks, 2nd Edition
intended_resources.author_year: Luc Perkins, Eric Redmond & Jim Wilson · 2018
intended_resources.rationale: Covers PostgreSQL, Redis, HBase, MongoDB, CouchDB, Cassandra, and Neo4j in one book. The approach of comparing databases side-by-side teaches you when to use which — the most valuable NoSQL skill. No other book builds this comparative intuition.

intended_resources.title: MongoDB for Developers — M101 (Free)
intended_resources.rationale: Official free MongoDB courses from MongoDB Inc. "M001: MongoDB Basics" and "M101: MongoDB for Developers" cover document model, CRUD, aggregation pipelines, and indexing. Pair with Redis University (redis.io/university) which is also free. Both are official certification prep.

intended_resources.title: MongoDB — The Complete Developer's Guide 2024
intended_resources.rationale: Most comprehensive MongoDB course — covers CRUD, aggregation, indexing, transactions, Atlas, and integration with Node/Python apps. Best paid resource for MongoDB depth before adding Redis and Cassandra for the broader NoSQL picture.

skills.name: Data Quality & Testing
skills.what_you_learn: data quality dimensions (completeness, accuracy, consistency, timeliness), Great Expectations (expectations, data docs, checkpoints), dbt tests, Soda Core for SQL-based quality checks, anomaly detection, data contracts, and building quality gates into pipelines before data reaches downstream consumers.

intended_resources.title: Fundamentals of Data Engineering (Ch. 9 — Data Quality)
intended_resources.rationale: No standalone book covers data quality as well as Reis & Housley's treatment in Chapter 9. For tool-specific depth, pair with the Great Expectations documentation (docs.greatexpectations.io) which is tutorial-quality. Together these cover the theory and practice completely.

intended_resources.title: Great Expectations Official Documentation & Tutorials
intended_resources.rationale: GX documentation is written as a practical tutorial series. The "Getting Started" through "How-to Guides" sections cover everything from first expectations to production data docs. Completely free, maintained by the GX team, includes Spark and SQL engine integrations.

intended_resources.title: Introduction to Data Quality in Python
intended_resources.rationale: Covers data quality assessment, profiling with pandas-profiling, validation with Great Expectations, and building quality pipelines. Best structured paid course for engineers new to data quality as a discipline rather than an afterthought.

skills.name: Cloud Platforms (AWS / GCP / Azure)
skills.what_you_learn: core compute (EC2/Cloud Run/VMs), object storage (S3/GCS/ADLS), IAM and permissions, networking (VPC, subnets, security groups), managed databases (RDS/Cloud SQL), serverless functions (Lambda/Cloud Functions), container registries, and cost management basics. Pick one cloud deeply.

intended_resources.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect Study Guide
intended_resources.rationale: AWS holds 31% cloud market share — learning AWS first maximizes job options. This study guide covers every core AWS service with architecture trade-offs. Even if you don't take the certification, this book gives you a complete mental model of cloud infrastructure.

intended_resources.title: AWS Skill Builder + Google Cloud Skills Boost (Free Tier)
intended_resources.rationale: Both AWS Skill Builder and Google Cloud Skills Boost offer free foundational courses. AWS has "Cloud Practitioner Essentials" free. Google offers free labs on core GCP services. Both include free tier sandbox environments to practice with real services.

intended_resources.title: Ultimate AWS Certified Solutions Architect Associate SAA-C03
intended_resources.rationale: Maarek is the top AWS instructor on Udemy with multiple AWS certifications. This course covers every AWS service with hands-on labs. Most engineers use this both to learn AWS and to pass the SAA-C03 exam — two outcomes for one course.

skills.name: Classical Machine Learning
skills.what_you_learn: linear/logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, gradient boosting (XGBoost/LightGBM), SVMs, k-means clustering, PCA, cross-validation, regularization (L1/L2), hyperparameter tuning with Scikit-learn's Pipeline API, and when to reach for deep learning vs classical methods.

intended_resources.title: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras & TensorFlow, 3rd Ed.
intended_resources.rationale: The best ML book for practitioners. Part 1 covers all classical ML algorithms through Scikit-learn. Géron's intuitive explanations are why this book is used in Google AI residency prep. The only ML book you need for classical methods — comprehensive and practical.

intended_resources.title: StatQuest Machine Learning Series
intended_resources.rationale: Every classical ML algorithm explained from mathematical first principles with animations. Josh covers regression, decision trees, random forests, gradient boosting, SVMs, PCA, clustering — all free. Watch the video for each algorithm before the Géron chapter on it.

intended_resources.title: Machine Learning Specialization
intended_resources.rationale: The most trusted ML course in the world. 3.6 million learners. Andrew Ng's intuition-first teaching style builds conceptual understanding before math. If you only take one paid ML course, this is it. Updated 2022 to include modern tools and Python.

skills.name: Deep Learning Fundamentals
skills.what_you_learn: perceptrons, activation functions (ReLU, sigmoid, softmax), forward pass, loss functions (MSE, cross-entropy), backpropagation chain rule, gradient descent (SGD, momentum, Adam, RMSprop), batch normalization, dropout, learning rate scheduling, and vanishing/exploding gradients.

intended_resources.title: Deep Learning
intended_resources.author_year: Goodfellow, Bengio & Courville · 2016 · Free at deeplearningbook.org
intended_resources.rationale: The academic foundation of deep learning. Dense and mathematical — use it as a reference, not a cover-to-cover read. Chapters 6–9 on feedforward networks, backprop, and regularization are the canonical source for these topics. Free online legally.

intended_resources.title: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
intended_resources.rationale: The best free deep learning course ever created. Karpathy (former Tesla AI Director, OpenAI) builds neural networks from scratch in pure Python/NumPy, then PyTorch, including a GPT from scratch. Every video is dense with insights that take years to acquire otherwise.

intended_resources.title: Deep Learning Specialization
intended_resources.rationale: 5 courses covering neural networks, optimization, hyperparameter tuning, CNNs, RNNs, and sequence models. 500,000+ completions. The most structured paid deep learning curriculum. Programming assignments in Python/NumPy build every component manually before using frameworks.

skills.name: PyTorch
skills.what_you_learn: tensors (creation, manipulation, broadcasting), autograd and computational graphs, nn.Module and nn.Sequential, custom Dataset and DataLoader, training loops with optimizer.step(), model saving/loading, moving models to GPU, torchvision, and debugging PyTorch models.

intended_resources.title: Deep Learning with PyTorch
intended_resources.author_year: Stevens, Antiga & Viehmann · Manning · 2020 · Free PDF
intended_resources.rationale: Written by PyTorch core contributors. Covers tensors, autograd, neural net construction, and real applications (image classification, NLP, generative models). Free PDF available from Manning's website with free account. The authoritative PyTorch book written by people who built it.

intended_resources.title: Learn PyTorch for Deep Learning — Zero to Mastery
intended_resources.rationale: The best free PyTorch course/book available. Bourke builds every PyTorch concept with runnable Colab notebooks and a companion YouTube video series. Covers tensors through transformers. Free, continually updated, and structured as a complete course.

intended_resources.title: PyTorch for Deep Learning Bootcamp
intended_resources.rationale: Covers PyTorch from tensors through CNNs, RNNs, and GANs with Jupyter notebooks for every section. Portilla's courses are known for clarity and depth. Best structured paid PyTorch course for engineers who learn best through video + notebooks.

skills.name: CNNs & Computer Vision
skills.what_you_learn: convolution operation, filters/feature maps, pooling, CNN architectures (LeNet, VGG, ResNet, EfficientNet), transfer learning (freezing layers, fine-tuning), data augmentation with torchvision/albumentations, object detection (YOLO, Faster R-CNN), and image segmentation basics.

intended_resources.title: Programming PyTorch for Deep Learning (CV chapters)
intended_resources.rationale: Chapters 3–6 cover CNNs and transfer learning in PyTorch with complete working code. Pair with Stanford's CS231n lecture notes for theoretical depth. For pure CV depth, the fast.ai book (free) is also excellent and goes further into practical techniques.

intended_resources.title: CS231n: Convolutional Neural Networks for Visual Recognition
intended_resources.author_year: Fei-Fei Li, Andrej Karpathy et al. · Stanford · cs231n.github.io
intended_resources.rationale: The most cited deep learning course for computer vision. Full lecture notes, slides, and assignments available free at cs231n.github.io. Covers CNNs, optimization, visualization, object detection, and segmentation. Written by the team that created ImageNet.

intended_resources.title: Convolutional Neural Networks (Course 4 of Deep Learning Specialization)
intended_resources.rationale: Covers CNN architectures, object detection (YOLO), face recognition, and neural style transfer with programming assignments in TensorFlow/Keras. Best structured paid CV course — practical assignments build real systems, not just train toy models.

skills.name: Transformers & NLP
skills.what_you_learn: self-attention mechanism, positional encoding, encoder-decoder architecture, BERT (masked language modeling, next sentence prediction), GPT (causal language modeling, autoregressive generation), tokenization (BPE, WordPiece), and fine-tuning pretrained models with HuggingFace.

intended_resources.title: Natural Language Processing with Transformers (Revised Ed.)
intended_resources.rationale: Written by HuggingFace engineers. Covers text classification, NER, QA, summarization, translation, and generation — all using the HuggingFace Transformers library. The definitive practical guide to transformers in production NLP pipelines.

intended_resources.title: HuggingFace NLP Course
intended_resources.rationale: Official free course from the team that built the Transformers library. Covers tokenizers, models, fine-tuning, and the HuggingFace Hub. Every chapter has free Colab notebooks. This is the most up-to-date free transformer resource because it's maintained by HuggingFace itself.

intended_resources.title: Natural Language Processing Specialization
intended_resources.rationale: 4 courses covering NLP with classification, probabilistic models, sequence models, and attention mechanisms. Builds from word vectors through transformers. Best structured paid curriculum for building NLP intuition before diving into HuggingFace.

skills.name: Model Evaluation & Metrics
skills.what_you_learn: classification metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1, AUC-ROC, AUC-PR), regression metrics (MAE, MSE, RMSE, R²), confusion matrix, cross-validation strategies (k-fold, stratified, time-series), calibration, statistical significance testing for model comparisons, and offline vs online evaluation frameworks.

intended_resources.title: Hands-On Machine Learning (Ch. 3 — Classification) + Designing ML Systems (Ch. 6)
intended_resources.rationale: No single book covers evaluation as well as these two chapters combined. Géron's Chapter 3 (Classification) is the best treatment of metrics for classical ML; Huyen's Chapter 6 covers evaluation for production ML systems including A/B testing and shadow deployment. Read both.

intended_resources.title: StatQuest — ROC and AUC, Precision/Recall, Confusion Matrices
intended_resources.rationale: Josh Starmer's videos on AUC-ROC and precision/recall are the clearest explanations of these concepts. His "ROC and AUC, Clearly Explained!" video (3M+ views) builds the geometric intuition that makes these metrics feel obvious rather than arbitrary.

intended_resources.title: Machine Learning in Production (MLOps Specialization — Course 1)
intended_resources.rationale: The first course of the MLOps specialization covers model evaluation in production — not just on a test set. Covers data drift, concept drift, slicing analysis, and evaluation infrastructure. Best paid resource for evaluation as a production engineering discipline.

skills.name: Feature Engineering
skills.what_you_learn: encoding categoricals (one-hot, target, embedding), scaling (standard, min-max, robust), handling missing data strategies, creating interaction features, time-series features (lag, rolling, Fourier), feature selection (mutual information, RFE), and feature stores (Feast, Tecton) for online/offline consistency.

intended_resources.title: Feature Engineering for Machine Learning
intended_resources.rationale: The only book entirely dedicated to feature engineering. Covers numerical, categorical, text, and image features with worked examples. Alice Zheng was a research scientist at Microsoft and Google. This skill determines model performance more than architecture choices — own it completely.

intended_resources.title: Feature Engineering Course — Kaggle Learn
intended_resources.rationale: Kaggle's free feature engineering course is practical and immediately applicable. Covers mutual information, creating features from domain knowledge, target encoding, and principal component analysis. Interactive Jupyter notebooks. Completely free. 4 hours to complete.

intended_resources.title: Feature Engineering for Machine Learning
intended_resources.author_year: Soledad Galli · Train in Data · Udemy
intended_resources.rationale: Soledad Galli (former HSBC quantitative analyst) is the leading educator on feature engineering. Covers every encoding and imputation technique with Python. Most comprehensive paid feature engineering course, especially strong for tabular/financial data.

skills.name: Experiment Tracking (MLflow / W&B)
skills.what_you_learn: logging hyperparameters, metrics, and artifacts, run comparison and visualization, model registry (MLflow), tagging and filtering experiments, integration with PyTorch/Scikit-learn training loops, hyperparameter sweeps (W&B Sweeps / MLflow Projects), and deploying a self-hosted MLflow tracking server.

intended_resources.title: Designing Machine Learning Systems (Ch. 6 — Model Development)
intended_resources.rationale: Huyen's Chapter 6 is the most thorough treatment of experiment management as a production engineering discipline. No standalone book covers MLflow + W&B as well as DMLS Chapter 6 combined with the official MLflow documentation (mlflow.org/docs), which is tutorial-quality.

intended_resources.title: W&B Courses — Effective MLOps: Model Development
intended_resources.rationale: Weights & Biases offers free courses built on their own platform. "Effective MLOps: Model Development" covers experiment tracking, model versioning, and sweeps using W&B. Best for engineers targeting companies that use W&B (OpenAI, NVIDIA, etc.). Completely free.

intended_resources.title: MLflow for ML Experiment Tracking
intended_resources.rationale: Covers MLflow tracking, projects, models, and registry with hands-on Python exercises. Includes deployment patterns. Best paid structured course for MLflow specifically — used more than W&B in enterprise/open-source production environments.

skills.name: HuggingFace Ecosystem
skills.what_you_learn: Transformers library (pipeline API, AutoModel/AutoTokenizer, Trainer API), Datasets library for efficient data loading, HuggingFace Hub (uploading/sharing models and datasets), PEFT library for efficient fine-tuning, Accelerate for distributed training, and Spaces for deploying Gradio/Streamlit ML demos.

intended_resources.title: Natural Language Processing with Transformers (Revised Ed.)
intended_resources.rationale: Written by HuggingFace engineers. Every code example uses the HuggingFace ecosystem. Chapter code available free on GitHub (github.com/nlp-with-transformers). This book IS the HuggingFace ecosystem book — the authors built the library being taught.

intended_resources.title: HuggingFace Deep RL Course + NLP Course
intended_resources.rationale: HuggingFace's own learn.huggingface.co offers multiple free courses. The NLP course and Deep RL course both use the HuggingFace ecosystem throughout. Always up to date with the latest library versions. Free, with free GPU compute via Colab integration.

intended_resources.title: Complete Generative AI Course With Langchain and HuggingFace
intended_resources.rationale: Covers HuggingFace Transformers, PEFT fine-tuning, LangChain integration, and deployment. Naik is one of the most active AI educators in the community. Best paid course for applying the HuggingFace ecosystem to real LLM applications beyond basic NLP tasks.

skills.name: MLOps & Model Deployment
skills.what_you_learn: model serialization (pickle, ONNX, TorchScript), serving frameworks (TorchServe, TF Serving, BentoML, FastAPI wrapper), containerizing models with Docker, monitoring predictions for drift, A/B testing model variants, shadow deployment, model registry workflows, and CI/CD for ML models.

intended_resources.title: Designing Machine Learning Systems
intended_resources.rationale: The best book on taking ML from prototype to production. Covers data pipelines, feature stores, model development, deployment, monitoring, and infrastructure. Every ML engineer needs to read this book. Chip Huyen advised companies including Snorkel AI, NVIDIA, and Netflix on ML systems.

intended_resources.title: Made With ML — MLOps Course
intended_resources.rationale: The best free end-to-end MLOps course. Goku Mohandas (former Apple, Google) builds a complete ML service from data annotation through model serving, monitoring, and CI/CD — all free. Covers FastAPI serving, Docker, testing ML code, and GitHub Actions for ML. Over 40,000 students.

intended_resources.title: Machine Learning Engineering for Production (MLOps) Specialization
intended_resources.rationale: 4 courses covering ML pipelines, feature engineering for production, model deployment, and model monitoring. Uses TFX (Google's production ML framework) with real industry patterns. The most systematic paid curriculum for ML production engineering.

skills.name: LLMs & Fine-Tuning (LoRA / RLHF)
skills.what_you_learn: LLM pretraining concepts (next-token prediction, tokenization, scaling laws), instruction fine-tuning, LoRA/QLoRA (low-rank adaptation for efficient fine-tuning), RLHF pipeline (reward model, PPO), PEFT library, quantization (4-bit, 8-bit), Axolotl/LLaMA-Factory for fine-tuning, and evaluating fine-tuned models.

intended_resources.title: Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch)
intended_resources.rationale: Builds a GPT-style LLM from scratch in Python/PyTorch — pretraining, instruction fine-tuning, and RLHF. Raschka is a research scientist at Lightning AI. The most technically rigorous LLM book for engineers who want to understand the full stack, not just use the API.

intended_resources.title: Let's build GPT: from scratch, in code, spelled out
intended_resources.rationale: The most watched and cited LLM tutorial. Karpathy builds a character-level GPT from scratch, explaining every line of code. Companion to his "Neural Networks: Zero to Hero" series. After this video, the Transformer architecture has no mystery. 3 hours, completely free.

intended_resources.title: Finetuning Large Language Models
intended_resources.author_year: Sharon Zhou · DeepLearning.AI (short course, low cost)
intended_resources.rationale: Covers full fine-tuning, LoRA, and RLHF concepts with hands-on Jupyter notebooks. Sharon Zhou (Stanford PhD, Lamini AI CEO) is the leading educator on LLM fine-tuning. Best paid practical course for LoRA/RLHF fine-tuning with working code. ~$49 on DeepLearning.AI.

skills.name: RAG & Vector Databases
skills.what_you_learn: embedding models (sentence-transformers, OpenAI embeddings), vector similarity search (cosine, dot product, L2), chunking strategies, vector databases (Pinecone, Weaviate, Chroma, pgvector), RAG pipeline architecture (retrieve → augment → generate), reranking, hybrid search, and evaluating RAG quality (RAGAS framework).

intended_resources.title: Building LLM Apps: A Practitioner's Guide
intended_resources.rationale: Covers RAG architectures, vector stores, LangChain, LlamaIndex, and evaluation frameworks for LLM applications. Most complete practical book for RAG pipeline engineering in 2024. Pair with the LlamaIndex documentation (docs.llamaindex.ai) which is excellent and free.

intended_resources.title: Building and Evaluating Advanced RAG — DeepLearning.AI Short Course
intended_resources.rationale: Free short course from DeepLearning.AI covering advanced RAG patterns. Builds sentence window retrieval, auto-merging retrieval, and RAG evaluation with RAGAS. All short courses on DeepLearning.AI are free. This is one of the most practical immediately applicable.

intended_resources.title: LangChain & Vector Databases in Production
intended_resources.rationale: Covers LangChain, vector databases (Deep Lake, Pinecone, Weaviate), embeddings, and building production RAG pipelines. Best paid course for end-to-end RAG application development with multiple vector DB options covered.

skills.name: Distributed Training
skills.what_you_learn: data parallelism (DDP — DistributedDataParallel), model parallelism (tensor/pipeline parallelism), ZeRO optimization stages (DeepSpeed), FSDP (Fully Sharded Data Parallel), gradient accumulation, mixed precision training (FP16/BF16), checkpoint sharding, and multi-node training on GPU clusters.

intended_resources.title: Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch) — Ch. on Training at Scale
intended_resources.rationale: Raschka's book includes dedicated sections on distributed training with PyTorch's DDP and FSDP. Pair with the DeepSpeed documentation (deepspeed.ai/docs) and PyTorch's official distributed training tutorials — together these three free/paid resources cover all distributed training scenarios.

intended_resources.title: HuggingFace Accelerate Documentation + PyTorch DDP Tutorial
intended_resources.rationale: HuggingFace Accelerate abstracts DDP/FSDP/DeepSpeed into a unified API — it's what most engineers actually use. The Accelerate docs are tutorial-quality. Pair with PyTorch's official DDP tutorial (pytorch.org/tutorials) for the underlying mechanics. Both free.

intended_resources.title: Training & Fine-tuning LLMs for Production (LLM Engineering)
intended_resources.rationale: Covers distributed fine-tuning of LLMs using DeepSpeed, FSDP, and QLoRA with W&B for tracking. Built by W&B engineers for production GPU cluster workflows. Best paid course for distributed training in the context of LLMs specifically.

skills.name: Distributed Systems (Advanced)
skills.what_you_learn: CAP theorem in practice, consistency models (linearizability, eventual, causal), distributed transactions (2PC, Saga), consensus algorithms (Raft, Paxos intuition), leader election, distributed clocks (vector clocks, Lamport timestamps), partition handling strategies, and designing for failure (circuit breakers, bulkheads, timeouts).

intended_resources.title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
intended_resources.rationale: Part 2 (Chapters 5–9) is the best treatment of distributed systems for practitioners ever written. Covers replication, partitioning, transactions, consistency, and consensus with real-world examples. This book is mandatory for any engineer targeting staff-level roles at Google, Meta, or Amazon.

intended_resources.title: MIT 6.824: Distributed Systems
intended_resources.author_year: Robert Morris et al. · MIT · pdos.csail.mit.edu/6.824
intended_resources.rationale: The most rigorous free distributed systems course available. Lecture videos, reading list (GFS, MapReduce, Raft, Spanner papers), and Go programming labs that implement Raft from scratch. Used as reference by Google and Amazon engineers preparing for staff-level interviews.

intended_resources.title: Grokking the Principles and Practices of Advanced System Design
intended_resources.rationale: Covers advanced distributed systems patterns — consistent hashing, distributed caching, coordination services, and real architectures (Dynamo, Cassandra, Spanner). Best paid resource for engineers transitioning from system design basics to distributed systems depth.

skills.name: Streaming Systems (Flink / Spark Streaming)
skills.what_you_learn: streaming vs micro-batch architecture, event time vs processing time, watermarks and late data handling, windows (tumbling, sliding, session), stateful stream processing, Apache Flink (DataStream API, Table API), Spark Structured Streaming, exactly-once semantics, and stream-table join patterns.

intended_resources.title: Streaming Systems
intended_resources.author_year: Tyler Akidau, Slava Chernyak & Reuven Lax · O'Reilly · 2018
intended_resources.rationale: Written by the Google Dataflow team — the people who invented the streaming model. Covers the Beam model (windows, watermarks, triggers, accumulation) in depth. This is the theoretical foundation for all streaming systems including Flink and Spark Structured Streaming.

intended_resources.title: Apache Flink Official Training + Flink Forward Talks
intended_resources.rationale: Apache Flink's official training documentation is tutorial-quality and free. The "Learn Flink" section covers DataStream API from basics to stateful processing. Supplement with Flink Forward conference talks on YouTube for production patterns used at Uber, Netflix, and Alibaba.

intended_resources.title: Apache Flink — Real-Time Data Engineering
intended_resources.rationale: Covers Flink DataStream API, Table API, Kafka integration, stateful processing, and deployment on Kubernetes. Best paid course for Flink specifically, covering the full stack from source to sink with real use cases (fraud detection, real-time analytics).

skills.name: Data Lakehouse (Iceberg / Delta Lake)
skills.what_you_learn: data lake vs data warehouse vs lakehouse architecture, open table formats (Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, Apache Hudi), ACID transactions on object storage, schema evolution, time travel / table versioning, partition evolution, metadata management, and connecting lakehouse tables to Spark/Flink/Trino.

intended_resources.title: Apache Iceberg: The Definitive Guide
intended_resources.author_year: Tomer Shiran, Jason Hughes & Alex Merced · O'Reilly · 2024
intended_resources.rationale: Written by Dremio engineers — the leading Iceberg contributors. Covers Iceberg architecture, table evolution, time travel, Spark/Flink integration, and comparison with Delta Lake and Hudi. Iceberg is winning the open table format war — this is the book to own it deeply.

intended_resources.title: Delta Lake Documentation + Databricks Academy Free Courses
intended_resources.rationale: Delta Lake documentation is tutorial-quality and free. Databricks Academy offers free "Data Engineering with Databricks" modules that cover Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, and lakehouse architecture. Free with account registration. Regularly updated for new Databricks features.

intended_resources.title: Apache Iceberg Crash Course: Data Lakehouse with Dremio & Spark
intended_resources.rationale: Alex Merced is a Developer Advocate at Dremio — he's one of the primary Iceberg educators in the community. Covers Iceberg with Spark, Flink, and Dremio hands-on. Best practical paid course for Iceberg specifically, taught by someone who works on it professionally.

skills.name: Observability & Monitoring
skills.what_you_learn: the three pillars (logs, metrics, traces), Prometheus metrics collection and PromQL, Grafana dashboards and alerting, structured logging with JSON, distributed tracing with Jaeger/Zipkin, OpenTelemetry instrumentation, SLOs and error budgets, on-call runbooks, and ML-specific monitoring (data drift, prediction drift, model performance degradation).

intended_resources.title: Site Reliability Engineering (Google SRE Book)
intended_resources.author_year: Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy · Google · Free at sre.google/books
intended_resources.rationale: The foundational text for monitoring, SLOs, and operational excellence. Chapters 4 (SLOs), 6 (Monitoring), and 12 (On-call) are the most referenced. Completely free at sre.google/books. How Google operates services at scale — monitoring is central to the entire SRE discipline.

intended_resources.title: Prometheus & Grafana Complete Tutorial
intended_resources.rationale: Best free video tutorial for setting up Prometheus + Grafana. Nana covers metrics collection, exporters, PromQL, alert rules, and dashboard creation in a Kubernetes environment. Her videos are exceptionally clear and practical. Pair with the OpenTelemetry documentation for distributed tracing.

intended_resources.title: Monitoring and Alerting with Prometheus
intended_resources.rationale: Covers Prometheus architecture, exporters, alertmanager, PromQL, recording rules, and Grafana integration with a Docker/Kubernetes lab environment. Best paid course for building a complete Prometheus-based observability stack from scratch in a real environment.

skills.name: Kubernetes Advanced / Helm
skills.what_you_learn: Helm chart authoring, templating, values files, chart repositories, RBAC (service accounts, roles, cluster roles), network policies, StatefulSets, persistent volumes, HPA/VPA for autoscaling, Kubernetes operators, GitOps with ArgoCD/Flux, admission controllers, and securing production clusters.

intended_resources.title: The Kubernetes Book (2024 Edition)
intended_resources.rationale: Updated annually. The most concise yet complete Kubernetes reference. Covers pods, deployments, services, storage, security, and Helm. Poulton's annual updates keep this the freshest Kubernetes book — critical in a fast-moving ecosystem. Pair with Helm's official documentation for chart authoring depth.

intended_resources.title: Kubernetes for Beginners + CKA Course Preview (KodeKloud Free)
intended_resources.rationale: KodeKloud has the best Kubernetes labs environment. The free tier includes Kubernetes fundamentals with a browser-based lab. Mumshad's CKA prep course is the most trusted Kubernetes certification resource. The lab environment simulates real cluster operations without any local setup.

intended_resources.title: Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) with Practice Tests
intended_resources.rationale: The CKA is the most respected Kubernetes certification. Mumshad's prep course covers all exam objectives plus advanced topics (Helm, operators, GitOps). The CKA itself validates advanced Kubernetes skills — this course both teaches and certifies simultaneously. Best ROI of any DevOps paid course.

study_plan.detail: Build: Python CLI tool that reads a CSV, runs SQLite queries, computes statistics (NumPy), outputs a visualization (matplotlib). Design + core functionality.
Add: proper error handling, unit tests (pytest), Git commits with meaningful messages, README documentation.
Polish + push to GitHub. Write a 1-page reflection: what you know, what's fuzzy, what's solid. Foundation COMPLETE.

project_sprints.name: SWE Project Sprint — Production REST API

study_plan.detail: Design a production REST API service: ERD, API spec (OpenAPI), auth flow, deployment plan.
FastAPI + PostgreSQL + Redis. Full auth, CRUD, async. Tests passing. Docker ready.
GitHub Actions pipeline: test → build → push → deploy to cloud. Monitoring with logs.
Documentation, README, OpenAPI docs, security audit, performance test. Push to GitHub. Done.
